artifact.name: OpenAI Codex
artifact.description: A terminal-oriented programming-agent system with interactive, automated, server, extension, and programmatic execution surfaces.

element.ef: Transforms software-development intent into iterative model-guided reasoning and actions against a working software artifact.

join.op: Maintain Codex conversations, turns, context, resumability, and ongoing execution state while coding work progresses.
join.observation: A conversational programming agent carries iterative task state through a session runtime.

entity.name: thread session runtime
entity.observation: A thread groups successive agent turns into one continuing conversation.

entity.name: history session runtime
entity.observation: Session history preserves prior interaction state for later continuation.

entity.name: context session runtime
entity.observation: Session context supplies prior interaction state to subsequent agent work.

join.op: Let Codex inspect files, run commands, search resources, modify the working tree, and perform other callable coding operations.
join.observation: A programming agent performs concrete work through callable tool operations.

entity.name: command tool runtime
entity.observation: A command tool runtime executes host commands and returns their results.

entity.name: patch tool runtime
entity.observation: A patch tool runtime transforms files from structured patch instructions.

entity.name: search tool runtime
entity.observation: A search tool runtime locates information requested during agent work.

join.op: Constrain Codex actions according to sandbox boundaries, approval decisions, and executable-operation policy.
join.observation: Agent-controlled host operations pass through execution controls before unrestricted effects are permitted.

entity.name: sandbox execution control
entity.observation: A sandbox limits the host resources available to an executing operation.

entity.name: approval execution control
entity.observation: Approval control determines whether an operation requiring additional authority may proceed.

entity.name: policy execution control
entity.observation: Execution policy classifies operations against configured rules before execution.

join.op: Expose Codex locally as both an interactive terminal experience and a non-interactive command suitable for scripted execution.
join.observation: A terminal programming agent exposes command-driven interaction for human or automated callers.

entity.name: interactive command interface
entity.observation: An interactive command interface exchanges incremental input and output with a human operator.

entity.name: automation command interface
entity.observation: An automation command interface supports unattended invocation and machine-consumable results.

join.op: Provide Codex agent lifecycle operations to richer clients without embedding the core runtime directly into each client surface.
join.observation: An application server presents agent lifecycle operations across a client-server boundary.

element.ef: Owns continuing conversational execution state and coordinates successive agent turns within that state.

join.op: Represent Codex thread, turn, item, request, and event state consistently across runtime boundaries.
join.observation: A session runtime exchanges lifecycle state through a defined session protocol.

join.op: Execute the model-requested operations belonging to each Codex turn.
join.observation: A session runtime dispatches requested operations to a tool runtime while a turn is active.

element.ef: Registers callable operations, resolves requested tools, and dispatches their execution to concrete handlers.

join.op: Apply Codex permission and execution restrictions before effectful tool operations reach the host environment.
join.observation: Tool operations that can affect host resources are mediated by execution controls.

join.op: Make Codex tool capabilities expandable through MCP servers, plugins, connectors, skills, and hooks.
join.observation: An extensible tool runtime can incorporate externally or separately defined capabilities into its callable catalog.

entity.name: MCP extension runtime
entity.observation: An MCP extension runtime discovers and invokes capabilities through Model Context Protocol servers.

entity.name: plugin extension runtime
entity.observation: A plugin extension runtime introduces separately packaged capabilities into a host runtime.

entity.name: connector extension runtime
entity.observation: A connector extension runtime exposes capabilities backed by external services.

entity.name: skill extension runtime
entity.observation: A skill extension runtime supplies reusable task guidance and supporting resources.

entity.name: hook extension runtime
entity.observation: A hook extension runtime invokes configured behavior at defined lifecycle events.

element.ef: Mediates host operations according to isolation boundaries, permission requirements, and executable-operation rules.
Presents agent capabilities as terminal commands with interactive and automation-oriented execution modes.

join.op: Drive Codex threads and turns from the TUI and exec surfaces through the shared in-process application-server lifecycle.
join.observation: Command surfaces can share an application-server lifecycle instead of independently implementing agent-session orchestration.

element.ef: Exposes agent lifecycle operations as structured requests, responses, notifications, and streamed state changes.

join.op: Create, resume, steer, inspect, and manage Codex threads and turns on behalf of client applications.
join.observation: An agent application server delegates conversational lifecycle operations to a session runtime.

join.op: Encode Codex application-server requests, responses, notifications, and lifecycle data in a stable typed contract.
join.observation: An application server communicates with clients through a defined request and event protocol.

element.ef: Defines typed representations for agent submissions, lifecycle requests, responses, notifications, events, and conversation state.
Lets host programs start, resume, run, and consume programming-agent conversations through a software API.

join.op: Let the Codex TypeScript SDK start or resume agent threads by invoking the packaged Codex executable and consuming its structured execution stream.
join.observation: A subprocess-backed programmatic client can expose a command-driven agent as a host-language API.

element.ef: Discovers, loads, and connects separately defined capabilities that augment the host agent runtime.

join.op: Expose enabled Codex extensions as capabilities the agent can discover or invoke during work.
join.observation: An extension runtime augments a host tool runtime with additional discoverable behavior.
